subtitle: When Stone Boasted and Empires Broke

panels.shot: low-angle wide of two weathered stone pillars rising over a hazy Malwa plain, ghostly visages of Yashodharman and Mihirakula looming on either side of the sky
panels.action: Yashodharman stands firm in royal armour on one side of the Sondani pillars, Mihirakula looms on the other like a dark storm-lord, the ancient Malwa landscape stretching beneath a crimson dawn.

dialogue.text: On two lonely pillars near Sondani, a Malwa king declares he bent the Huna tempest; yet other memories whisper that Mihirakula’s fall was shared—whose victory do these stones truly sing?

i18n.hi: सोंदणी के पास दो अकेले स्तंभों पर एक मालवा राजा गरजता है कि उसने हूणों के तूफान को झुका दिया; पर यादों की सरसराहट कहती है, मिहिरकुला की हार कई हाथों की थी — तो ये पत्थर सच में किसकी जीत गाते हैं?

panels.shot: bird's-eye over the central Ganga plain and northwestern India, with faint overlays of shifting frontiers like ghostly lines
panels.action: An ancient map-like vista of northwestern India and the Ganga heartland appears as a living landscape, cities and rivers glowing faintly under a restless sky.

dialogue.text: In the fifth and sixth centuries, the land between the western marches and the Ganga plain rocked under new hooves and new banners. The Guptas reeled, and a Huna wind screamed across the frontier.

i18n.hi: पाँचवीं–छठी शताब्दी में पश्चिमी सरहदों से गंगा के मैदान तक नया खूर और नए झंडे गूँज उठे। गुप्त डगमगाए, और हूणों का तूफ़ानी झोंका सीमा पर चीखता चला गया।

panels.shot: dramatic split-panel style composition: on one side Toramana and Mihirakula’s Huna riders surge, on the other a Gupta standard buckles
panels.action: On one side, Mihirakula rides at the head of armoured horsemen under fluttering Huna standards; on the other, a weary Gupta officer lowers a battle-torn royal banner in a ruined fort.

dialogue.text: Toramana and his son Mihirakula, Huna lords from beyond the old frontiers, smashed through weakened Gupta lines. Cities burned, tribute shifted, and Malwa felt the thunder first.

i18n.hi: पुरानी सरहदों के उस पार से आए हूण सरदार तोरमाण और उसका बेटा मिहिरकुला, टूटे‑कमज़ोर गुप्त मोर्चों को चकनाचूर कर गए। शहर जले, नज़राने बदले, और सबसे पहले मालवा ने यह गड़गड़ाहट महसूस की।

panels.shot: medium shot of Mihirakula in a fort-like setting, his profile lit by torchlight, inscriptions faint behind him
panels.action: Mihirakula stands within a stone hall, hand resting on a pillar carved with early inscriptions, his face hard and intent as flames flicker along the walls.

dialogue.text: In later Gwalior stone, Mihirakula stands not as myth but as ruler—named, remembered, a king who carved his own claim on Indian soil long before any defeat.

i18n.hi: बाद की ग्वालियर शिला में मिहिरकुला कहानी नहीं, राजा है — नाम समेत, याद किया गया, एक शासक जिसने हार से बहुत पहले भारत की मिट्टी पर अपना दावा खुद तराशा।

panels.shot: wide shot of Malwa plateau with Mandsaur in the distance, a modest court scene gathering around a young Yashodharman
panels.action: On the Malwa plateau near Mandsaur, Yashodharman sits in a simple but dignified court, advisors around him, the frontier’s rugged hills visible beyond the open hall.

dialogue.text: In Malwa, as Gupta suzerainty cracked, a regional king rose—Yashodharman of Mandsaur. To some, he was a mere frontier lord; to his own poets, he was a storm waiting to answer another storm.

i18n.hi: मालवा में, जब गुप्त अधिराज्य की पकड़ ढीली पड़ी, एक प्रादेशिक राजा उभरा — मन्दसौर का यशोधर्मन। कुछ की नज़र में बस सरहद का ठाकुर; अपने कवियों के लिए, एक तूफान जो किसी दूसरे तूफ़ान का जवाब देने को तैयार था।

panels.shot: slow push-in on Yashodharman’s face as a messenger kneels before him in the court
panels.action: A dust-covered messenger kneels before Yashodharman, hands raised in supplication, while the king listens, brows drawn, jaw set.

dialogue.text: From the north came tidings of Mihirakula’s harsh rule and advancing power. Yashodharman faced a choice: bend, as many had, or stand, with Malwa as the stake.

i18n.hi: उत्तर से खबरें आईं — मिहिरकुला की कठोर हुकूमत और बढ़ती ताकत की। यशोधर्मन के सामने फ़ैसला था: झुक जाए, जैसे औरों ने किया, या डट जाए, मालवा को दाँव पर रखकर।

panels.shot: wide, dust-level shot of opposing armies mustering on an open field, banners of Malwa and Huna forces distinct
panels.action: On a broad plain, Yashodharman’s forces in orderly ranks face the advancing Huna cavalry under Mihirakula, dust hanging like a veil between the two armies.

dialogue.speaker: yashodharman_and_mihirakula
dialogue.text: “This land has bent enough,” Yashodharman murmurs. “Today, it will stand.”

i18n.hi: “यह धरती काफी झुक चुकी,” यशोधर्मन बुदबुदाता है। “आज, यह खड़ी होगी।”

panels.shot: dynamic overhead of chaotic battle lines clashing, with focus on Yashodharman and Mihirakula at a distance within the swirl
panels.action: Lines of infantry and cavalry crash together in swirling motion, Yashodharman directing from the centre while Mihirakula drives his horse along the Huna front.

dialogue.text: The Sondani inscription will not name the field, nor number the fallen. It will only remember this: that in one hard-fought clash, the Huna surge broke against Malwa’s line.

i18n.hi: सोंदणी की लेखी न मैदान का नाम बताएगी, न गिरने वालों की गिनती। बस इतना याद रखेगी: कि एक कठोर भिड़ंत में हूणों का उफान मालवा की रेखा से टकरा कर टूट गया।

panels.shot: medium shot of Mihirakula’s mounted figure turning away from the field, his army in disarray behind him
panels.action: Mihirakula rides away from a disordered field, his horse reined sharply, while scattered riders and broken formations trail behind.

dialogue.text: We cannot see the exact maneuvers now, only their echo: Mihirakula’s momentum checked, his power in the western land fractured, the myth of Huna invincibility suddenly thinner.

i18n.hi: आज हम चालें नहीं देख पाते, बस उनकी गूँज: मिहिरकुला की रफ़्तार थमी, पश्चिमी धरती पर उसकी ताकत चिरी, हूणों की अजेयता की कहानी अचानक पतली पड़ गई।

panels.shot: low-angle of masons at Sondani raising a freshly carved pillar, Yashodharman watching
panels.action: At Sondani, artisans haul an immense stone pillar upright with ropes, while Yashodharman watches from a platform, robes stirring in the river breeze.

dialogue.text: In the aftermath, Yashodharman chose stone as his witness. Near Sondani, close to Mandsaur, he raised two pillars and carved into them a victory song over Mihirakula.

i18n.hi: लड़ाई के बाद, यशोधर्मन ने पत्थर को गवाह चुना। सोंदणी के पास, मन्दसौर के नज़दीक उसने दो स्तंभ खड़े किए और उन पर मिहिरकुला पर जीत का गीत उकेरा।

panels.shot: extreme close-up of the Sondani pillar inscription lines, chisel poised over the stone
panels.action: A sculptor’s hand holds a chisel ready over the unfinished inscription, the early characters already biting deep into the pillar’s surface.

dialogue.text: The prashasti boasts that from the Lauhitya in the east to the western ocean, rulers bowed to him. It names Mihirakula, and declares that this frontier king humbled the Huna lord.

i18n.hi: प्रशस्ति शेखी बघारती है कि लोहित्य के पूर्व से लेकर पश्चिमी सागर तक शासक उसके आगे झुके। वह मिहिरकुला का नाम लेती है, और एलान करती है कि इस सरहदी राजा ने हूण नरेश को नीचा दिखाया।

panels.shot: split composition showing on one side a vast subcontinent under his name, on the other a more modest Malwa-centered domain
panels.action: On one side of the panel, an idealised map shows the subcontinent under Yashodharman’s reach; on the other, a more realistic map highlights only Malwa and its neighbours.

dialogue.text: Yet the inscription is also royal pride, stretching his suzerainty from ocean to ocean. The record outside Malwa is quieter; no empire of that size under Yashodharman can be firmly traced.

i18n.hi: पर शिलालेख राजगर्व भी है, जो उसके अधिराज्य को सागर से सागर तक फैलाता है। मालवा से बाहर का लेखा ज्यादा शांत है; इतने बड़े राज्य की हुकूमत यशोधर्मन के नाम पर साफ नहीं मिलती।

panels.shot: medium shot of Mihirakula in another court, distant from Malwa, with attendants around him
panels.action: In a different city’s court, Mihirakula sits on a throne, visibly older yet still imposing, courtiers gathered cautiously around him.

dialogue.text: For the story does not end for Mihirakula at Sondani. The Gwalior inscription and later memories show him still a king, still carving his name, even after Malwa slipped from his grasp.

i18n.hi: क्योंकि सोंदणी पर मिहिरकुला की कहानी खत्म नहीं होती। ग्वालियर के लेख और बाद की यादें उसे अब भी राजा दिखाती हैं, अब भी अपना नाम तराशते हुए, भले ही मालवा उसकी मुट्ठी से फिसल चुका था।

panels.shot: wide shot of Nalanda-like eastern cityscape with Baladitya and Mihirakula’s shadow in the distance
panels.action: An eastern city with monasteries and high walls rises under a cloudy sky, a king like Baladitya shown in council while a faint, looming silhouette of Mihirakula watches from afar.

dialogue.text: Centuries later, the Chinese monk Xuanzang would hear another tale: of Baladitya in the east defeating Mihirakula and sparing his life, letting a humbled Huna depart instead of die.

i18n.hi: सदियों बाद चीनी भिक्षु श्वेनत्सांग एक और किस्सा सुनेगा: पूरब में बलदित्य ने मिहिरकुला को हराया और जान बख्श दी — हारा हुआ हूण मारने के बजाय वापसी को छोड़ दिया गया।

panels.shot: moody Kashmir valley vista with Kalhana as a shadowy scribe figure writing by lamplight
panels.action: The Kashmir valley lies serene under snow-kissed peaks, while in the foreground Kalhana, imagined as a thoughtful scribe, writes by a small lamp.

dialogue.text: In twelfth-century Kashmir, Kalhana’s Rajatarangini guarded yet another memory: of Mihirakula in the north, a harsher ruler, whose end came in another landscape, under other kings.

i18n.hi: बारहवीं सदी के कश्मीर में कल्हण की राजतरंगिणी एक तीसरी याद सँभालती है: उत्तर में मिहिरकुला का, ज़्यादा सख्त शासक का, जिसकी अंत कथा किसी और भूभाग, किसी और राजाओं के साये में लिखी गई।

panels.shot: cross-fade style composition of three texts: Sondani pillars, Gwalior inscription, and a palm-leaf manuscript of Xuanzang’s work
panels.action: Three records appear side by side: the Sondani pillars, a stone slab like Gwalior’s, and a palm-leaf manuscript, each glowing faintly in the dark.

dialogue.text: Put together, these scattered voices agree on this much: Mihirakula was real and mighty; Yashodharman’s victory real and sharp; and after these clashes, the Huna storm lost its deep push into India.

i18n.hi: इन बिखरी आवाज़ों को जोड़ो तो इतना तो साफ है: मिहिरकुला सच था और प्रबल; यशोधर्मन की जीत सच थी और धारदार; और इन टक्करों के बाद हूणों का तूफान भारत के भीतर की गहराई तक धकेलने की ताकत खो बैठा।

panels.shot: wide shot of post-Gupta India, multiple regional thrones lit while the Gupta centre fades
panels.action: The subcontinent is shown again, this time with several regional courts glowing—Malwa, the northwest, the eastern realms—while the once-unified Gupta centre dims.

dialogue.text: Gupta power, already weakening, did not return. Instead, regional kings rose in the spaces the Hunas and the old empire had torn open. Yashodharman’s brief blaze was part of that great shifting.

i18n.hi: गुप्त शक्ति, जो पहले ही ढलान पर थी, वापस न आई। उसकी जगह उन दरारों में प्रादेशिक राज उभरे, जो हूणों और पुराने साम्राज्य ने मिलकर चिरी थीं। यशोधर्मन की क्षणिक ज्वाला उसी बड़ी करवट का हिस्सा थी।

panels.shot: present-day style shot of the weathered Sondani pillars under an open sky, small human figures dwarfed by them
panels.action: The Sondani pillars stand alone in a quiet field under a clear sky, a few tiny visitors walking at their base, dwarfed by the stone.

dialogue.text: Today, the Sondani pillars are weathered, their words partly worn, but they still carry that bold claim: that a Malwa king once made even Mihirakula bow, if only for a moment.

i18n.hi: आज सोंदणी के स्तंभ घिसे‑पिटे हैं, शब्द आधे मिटे, पर अब भी वही दिलेर दावा उठाए हुए हैं: कि एक मालवा राजा ने कभी मिहिरकुला जैसे शासक को भी झुकाया था, चाहे पल भर को ही सही।

panels.shot: close, contemplative shot of Yashodharman and Mihirakula’s ghostly profiles facing each other over the pillars
panels.action: Translucent, larger-than-life visages of Yashodharman and Mihirakula face each other in the sky above the pillars, their expressions complex—pride, defiance, and the quiet of history.

dialogue.text: Their clash reminds us that victory is not only in one king’s boast, but in how many voices we dare to hear; power passes, but the pillars endure, testing pride against evidence for every new age.

i18n.hi: उनकी टक्कर याद दिलाती है कि जीत सिर्फ एक राजा की डींग में नहीं, उन आवाज़ों में है जिन्हें हम सुनने का साहस करते हैं; ताकत गुजर जाती है, पर स्तंभ टिके रहते हैं, हर नयी उम्र में घमंड को सबूत से परखते हुए।

subtitle_i18n.en: When Stone Boasted and Empires Broke
